“With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen.” This stance—keeping rates at 0–0.25% with ongoing asset purchases under average-inflation targeting—is consistent with research showing that credible, rule-like policy helps anchor expectations (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and that forward guidance plus QE ease financial conditions at the zero lower bound. The use of interest on reserves supports rate control in a floor system (Goodfriend, 2002), while commitment devices like average-inflation targeting help mitigate inflation bias (Barro and Gordon), all pointing to a net supportive but still cautious outlook given pandemic-related risks noted by the Committee.
